messages:
Claire (Finance): We received an invoice from NordicSynth (vendor NS-PL-004). Marked 'reverse charge - recipient liable (Art. 28b)'. VAT ID PL1234567890. Net EUR 4,800. They also included a line 'Please gross-up 5% withholding if applicable' — do we need to gross-up? Thoughts?
Priya (Accounts Payable): Reverse charge means we account for VAT in our books (if we have an EU VAT number). Which Redwood entity is on the invoice? If it's the Dublin entity, reverse charge probably applies. W-9/W-8 are US forms — not relevant here.
Tomasz (Vendor Ops): Vendor says they billed our Dublin office (Redwood EMEA Ltd). Their email mentions Polish tax counsel suggesting a 5% withholding on certain cross-border service fees, but they didn't attach any certificate or legal reference.
Marta (Legal): Two separate items: VAT reverse charge and alleged Polish withholding. For reverse charge we need our EU VAT number on the invoice and a clear statement (or phrase) referencing the reverse charge. For withholding: vendor must provide Certificate of Tax Residence (CORT) and cite the legal basis. If they ask us to gross-up, that's a contract amendment and needs Legal + Finance sign-off.
TaxBot: Automated check: PL VAT ID PL1234567890 matches format. If billed to an Irish VAT-registered entity, reverse charge is standard and vendor should zero-rate the VAT. Polish withholding on cross-border B2B services is not automatic; vendor should supply CORT and remittance proof if they claim tax was or will be withheld. Recommend hold payment until docs are supplied.
Claire (Finance): Action items: 1) Tomasz request CORT + reissued invoice referencing reverse charge + confirmation of invoiced Redwood entity; 2) Priya will block payment; 3) Marta will review if they insist on gross-up and run the legal analysis.
Tomasz (Vendor Ops): Message sent to vendor (copied here):
```
Hi NordicSynth,

Thanks for the invoice. To process we need the following within 72 hours:
1) Certificate of Tax Residence (CORT) or official tax clearance;
2) A reissued invoice that breaks out VAT or explicitly states "reverse charge - recipient liable (Art. 28b)" and references applicable EU law;
3) Confirmation of which Redwood legal entity is the invoice recipient (please include our EU VAT number if applicable);
4) If you expect Redwood to gross-up, provide the legal basis, treaty references (if any), and a worked example calculation.

We will hold payment until we receive the above.

Thanks,
Tomasz
```
Priya (Accounts Payable): Blocking payment in AP now and flagging the invoice for tax review. Claire, please DM the exact entity/VAT info so I can match in the system.
Claire (Finance): DMing now: Redwood EMEA Ltd, VAT IE9999999FH. Will update here when vendor replies. :mag:
